blocks.text: Correlation handled the numeric feature, numeric target case well, but genuinely cannot apply to categorical data, there is no meaningful correlation coefficient between two sets of category labels. Chi-square fills that exact gap directly, a genuine statistical test built specifically to measure whether a categorical feature and a categorical target are actually related, or genuinely independent of each other.

This topic covers how chi-square genuinely builds directly on the cross tabulation first introduced in Bivariate Analysis, how it compares observed counts against what would genuinely be expected under independence, how to read the resulting statistic and its accompanying p-value, the real, practical requirement that chi-square needs non-negative count data specifically, and how to apply it directly with scikit-learn.
1. Building Directly on the Cross Tabulation

blocks.alt: Building Directly on the Cross Tabulation
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443280187-442461877.png

Chi-square genuinely starts from the exact same cross tabulation, or contingency table, first introduced back in Bivariate Analysis, counting how many rows fall into every genuine combination of a categorical feature and a categorical target. That table of counts is genuinely the direct, raw input chi-square actually computes from.

This is worth being explicit about, chi-square is not some unrelated, new statistical idea, it is genuinely a precise, quantified way of asking the exact same question that cross tabulation first made visible, do these two categorical variables actually relate to each other.
2. Observed Versus Expected Counts
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443280187-757348981.png

Chi-square genuinely compares the actual, observed counts in each cell of the cross tabulation against the counts that would genuinely be expected if the feature and target were truly independent, no real relationship at all. If location and purchased were genuinely unrelated, the proportion of purchases should genuinely look the same across every location category.

A genuinely large gap between what was actually observed and what pure independence would predict suggests a real, meaningful relationship exists. A genuinely small gap suggests the categories are behaving close to what independence alone would produce, with no real signal to speak of.
3. Reading the Chi-Square Statistic
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443280187-754034811.png

The chi-square statistic itself is genuinely a single number summarizing how large the gap between observed and expected counts actually is, across every cell in the table at once. A genuinely high chi-square statistic indicates a stronger real relationship between the feature and target, while a genuinely low statistic suggests little to no real relationship.

For feature selection specifically, features genuinely get ranked by this statistic, exactly the same top-k selection logic covered back in Filter Methods, just using chi-square as the specific scoring function instead of correlation.

blocks.text: 4. A Worked Example
Applying scikit-learn SelectKBest with the chi2 scoring function shows this technique directly, on a small dataset of encoded categorical features.

code.content:
from sklearn.feature_selection import SelectKBest, chi2
import pandas as pd

X = pd.DataFrame({
    "location_city": [1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0],
    "location_suburb": [0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1],
    "unrelated_flag": [1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0],
})
y = pd.Series([1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0])

selector = SelectKBest(score_func=chi2, k=2)
selector.fit(X, y)

print("Chi-square scores:", selector.scores_)
print("Selected:", X.columns[selector.get_support()].tolist())

blocks.text: The two location columns, genuinely tied directly to the target pattern here, receive genuinely high chi-square scores and get selected, while unrelated_flag, deliberately constructed with no real relationship to the target, genuinely receives a much lower score.

blocks.text: 5. The Real Requirement: Non-Negative Counts
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443280188-741671054.png

Chi-square genuinely requires non-negative input values, since it is fundamentally built around comparing counts, and a negative count genuinely makes no real, sensible meaning at all. This means chi-square genuinely fits naturally with the one-hot or ordinal encoded categorical features covered back in the Encoding Techniques module, which naturally produce non-negative values.

It genuinely cannot be applied directly to standardized features, covered in the Feature Scaling module, since standardization deliberately centers values around zero, producing genuinely negative numbers for roughly half of any typical feature.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: Never apply chi-square directly to standardized or otherwise negative valued features. It genuinely requires non-negative counts, exactly the kind produced by the encoding techniques covered earlier in this course.

blocks.text: 6. Interpreting the Accompanying P-Value
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443280188-855393845.png

Alongside the chi-square statistic itself, a genuine p-value indicates how likely the observed relationship could have occurred purely by random chance, if the feature and target were genuinely, truly independent. A genuinely low p-value, conventionally below 0.05, suggests the detected relationship is genuinely unlikely to be random noise, while a genuinely high p-value suggests it well might be.

This p-value adds a genuinely useful, additional layer of confidence beyond the raw chi-square statistic alone, helping distinguish a real, meaningful relationship from one that merely looks strong due to a small, genuinely noisy sample.
7. Applying This With scikit-learn
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443280188-539775124.png

SelectKBest with score_func set to chi2, exactly as shown in the worked example above, genuinely computes the chi-square statistic for every feature against the target and selects the genuinely top scoring ones, following the exact same interface pattern already established for correlation based selection in the previous topic.

This genuine consistency across scikit-learn feature selection tools is worth appreciating directly, moving between different filter method scoring functions requires learning only one shared, familiar interface, not several unrelated ones.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: Encode categorical features first, using the techniques from Encoding Techniques, before running chi2 through SelectKBest. Raw text category labels genuinely will not work directly.

blocks.text: 8. Chi-Square Versus What Comes Next
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443280188-683200835.png

Correlation and chi-square together now cover two of the three genuine variable type combinations feature selection needs to handle, numeric to numeric, and categorical to categorical. One genuine combination remains, a numeric feature against a categorical target, exactly the classification scenario this course covers in real depth soon.

The next topic, ANOVA, completes that final gap directly, a genuine statistical test built specifically for measuring whether a numeric feature genuinely differs meaningfully across the different classes of a categorical target.

items: Chi-square genuinely tests whether a categorical feature and categorical target are actually related or independent.
It builds directly on the cross tabulation counts first introduced back in Bivariate Analysis.
A genuinely high chi-square statistic indicates a stronger real relationship, used to rank features.
Chi-square genuinely requires non-negative counts, fitting naturally with one-hot or ordinal encoded features.
The accompanying p-value indicates whether a detected relationship is genuinely unlikely to be random chance.
The next topic, ANOVA, completes the third variable combination, numeric feature against categorical target.
